projects.flight: Flown summer 2026 aboard World View high-altitude balloons and Virgin Galactic suborbital spacecraft
projects.kidFriendly: Sixty student teams from across the United States won the chance to build real space experiments. Some of their inventions — like a device designed to heal scratches on spacecraft — flew in summer 2026 on balloons that rose nearly 100,000 feet and on a Virgin Galactic suborbital spaceship. It's proof that kids' ideas can really reach space!
projects.name: NASA TechRise Student Challenge — 2025–2026 Winning Experiments
projects.org: NASA (Flight Opportunities program) with Future Engineers

projects.flight: Challenge open Sept 3 – Nov 2, 2026; winners announced Jan 19, 2027; experiments fly on a high-altitude balloon in summer 2027
projects.kidFriendly: NASA is inviting 6th–12th graders to dream up a new space experiment. Winning teams get $1,500, a starter kit, and coaching to build their idea — and the best experiments will fly on a giant high-altitude balloon in summer 2027. Entries are due November 2, 2026, so there's still time to join!
projects.name: NASA TechRise Student Challenge — 2026–2027
projects.org: NASA (Flight Opportunities program) with Future Engineers

projects.flight: Launched October 13, 2026 aboard SpaceX CRS-35 (Falcon 9 + Cargo Dragon) from Cape Canaveral
projects.kidFriendly: Five Florida Tech engineering students are testing a special gel that might one day shield astronauts from space radiation. Their experiment rode to the International Space Station aboard a SpaceX cargo rocket on October 13, 2026. If the gel holds together in zero gravity, it could help keep future Moon and Mars explorers safe.
projects.name: Florida Tech Hydrogel Radiation-Shielding Experiment
projects.org: Florida Institute of Technology (Student Spaceflight Experiments Program)

projects.flight: Launched October 13, 2026 aboard SpaceX CRS-35 (Falcon 9 + Cargo Dragon) from Cape Canaveral
projects.kidFriendly: Four undergrads at the University of South Florida created a gel that helps cuts and wounds heal — even under a spacesuit. Two of their tiny lab tubes launched to the International Space Station on October 13, 2026, where astronauts will mix the ingredients in zero gravity. Back on Earth, the students will compare the space-made gel to one made in their lab.
projects.name: USF Wound-Healing Hydrogel Experiment (SSEP Mission 21)
projects.org: University of South Florida (Student Spaceflight Experiments Program, Mission 21)

projects.flight: Launch Day scheduled April 10, 2027 in Huntsville, Alabama (NASA Student Launch culminating event)
projects.kidFriendly: A team of five young rocketeers from Montville, New Jersey won national and international rocket contests in 2025 — and NASA just picked them for Student Launch. Over nine months they'll design and build a reusable high-power rocket, present their work to real NASA engineers, and launch it in Huntsville, Alabama.
projects.name: Troop 74 Rocketeers — NASA Student Launch
projects.org: NASA Marshall Space Flight Center (team: BSA Montville Troop 74, New Jersey)

projects.flight: Launched early October 2026 aboard a SpaceX Falcon 9 from Vandenberg; nine-month student-operated mission now underway in orbit (~500 km)
projects.kidFriendly: Georgia Tech students spent three years building a tiny satellite with a brand-new kind of engine — one fuel source that can power both quick bursts and super-efficient cruising. It reached orbit in early October 2026, and now students fly it themselves from a mission control room right on campus. Over nine months they'll steer it through more than 1,000 hours of engine tests.
projects.name: ASCENT Propulsion Dual Mode CubeSat
projects.org: Georgia Tech Space Systems Design Laboratory with NASA

projects.flight: Launched April 11, 2026 aboard Northrop Grumman NG-24 (Cygnus); deployed into orbit from the ISS
projects.kidFriendly: Six tiny satellites built by U.S. schools and nonprofit groups — with fun names like Coconut, HUCSat, and LEOPARDSat-1 — rode to the International Space Station on NASA's NG-24 cargo mission in April 2026. Each was then released into orbit to run its own experiment. Small satellites, big science!
projects.name: ELaNa 58 Student CubeSats (Coconut, HUCSat, LEOPARDSat-1, PROVES ×3)
projects.org: NASA CubeSat Launch Initiative (six CubeSats built by U.S. universities and nonprofits)

projects.flight: Most recent flight June 24, 2026 (Terrier-Improved Malemute, Wallops Island); annual program — next flight date to be announced
projects.kidFriendly: Every year, college students from across the country design experiments that fly on a real NASA sounding rocket from Wallops, Virginia. On June 24, 2026, nearly 50 experiments from 38 teams soared about 100 miles up, then parachuted into the Atlantic Ocean to be picked up. The next annual launch cycle is already underway.
projects.name: NASA RockSat / RockOn Student Sounding Rockets
projects.org: NASA Wallops Flight Facility with the Colorado and Virginia Space Grant Consortia
